speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing sudden-onset vertigo; to help me narrow down the cause, have you noticed any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or difficulty with your balance?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: That was a very brief episode lasting only three minutes, and you are now back to your baseline. Did the spinning sensation worsen or improve when you moved your head or turned in bed? Also, did you notice any new hearing loss or tinnitus (ringing) during this episode?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The brief duration (3 minutes) and lack of persistent hearing loss or tinnitus strongly suggest an inner ear crystal disorder rather than Meniere's or a central cause. I will now request a Dix-Hallpike test to confirm the diagnosis.
